chunks: And it is narrated from ʿUmar ibn Yazīd, the seller of Sābirī, who said:
I said to Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام: “May I be your ransom! The people claim that profit taken from one who is compelled is forbidden, and that it is from usury.” So he said:
“Have you ever seen anyone, rich or poor, purchase except out of necessity, O ʿUmar? Indeed,”
“Allah has permitted trade and forbidden usury.”
“So make a profit, but do not practice usury.”
I said: “And what is usury?” He said: “Dirhams for dirhams, two like for one like.”

key_terms.الرِّبَا: usury; prohibited increase in certain exchanges
key_terms.الرِّبْحَ: lawful profit or gain made through trade
key_terms.الْبَيْعَ: trade or sale that is lawful in principle
key_terms.الْمُضْطَرِّ: a person under compulsion or necessity
key_terms.دَرَاهِمُ: silver coins used here as an example of monetary exchange

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between lawful profit in trade and riba in this hadith of Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith distinguishes lawful commercial profit from prohibited riba. Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام cites the Qur'anic principle that Allah has permitted trade and forbidden usury, clarifying that gain in sale is allowed while riba lies in usurious monetary exchange.
